blocks.text: In verses 1–5, “servant” explicitly names Jacob or Israel, while the promise also embraces a plural community through Israel’s descendants. Elsewhere in Isaiah, singular servant passages have been understood in several ways—collectively, individually, prophetically, royally, or messianically—and the language does not by itself settle every later identification.

The naming of Cyrus at the chapter’s close opens into a wider passage that calls him YHWH’s shepherd and anointed agent in relation to Babylon’s defeat and Jerusalem’s restoration. This description does not portray Cyrus as an Israelite Davidic king. The wider setting and development of these passages remain debated.
